title: The Other Energy Shock
gist: Gavekal's Wei He says China is hiding a domestic coal-supply shock, caused by a post-accident Shanxi safety drive, behind its claims of energy resilience during $100 oil from the Iran conflict.

insights.claim: Oil is only 18% of China's energy consumption and coal over half, which officials credit for escaping the oil shortages seen elsewhere during the Iran conflict with oil above $100 a barrel.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: China's insulation from the oil shock rests on coal supply.

insights.claim: China is experiencing a domestic coal-supply shock: a sweeping safety drive after a major Shanxi mining accident has depressed output and raised coal prices.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Higher coal prices feed China's power and industrial costs.

insights.claim: Chinese policymakers chose to restrict coal supply despite its role as the system stabilizer, showing they tolerate higher energy prices and slower growth to pursue other policy aims and the domestic political cycle.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Treat Chinese policy as less growth-maximizing than assumed.
